semantics.pathIsolation: Each path projects its own sequence from the shared step registry; all panel state is folded from initial state within that path. Taking Next after selecting a path preserves that path. Selecting a shared step chip can select a different path. See rendererReferences.pathIsolation.
semantics.fieldMerge: Device-app field patches merge individual properties with prior values within the selected path; omitted value/status/detail/visible are carried. A null field patch resets value to null, status unknown, detail empty and source null. See rendererReferences.fieldMerge.
semantics.phoneScreenVisibility: phoneScreen home renders the clock, notification cards and decorative launcher, but no device-app field cards. Stored fields still fold while hidden and may appear on a later app screen. The independent source-provenance cards can show field names and status while home, but not those field values. phoneScreen app renders only fields whose merged visible property is not false. See homeVsApp, fieldCardVisibility and sourceCardIndependentOfScreen renderer references.
semantics.visibleInPhoneMeans: renderedAsCard means a field card exists under the current phoneScreen and panel visibility. It does not assert intersection with the browser viewport or the phone inner scrollport. browser.json records actual card/scrollport intersection independently.
semantics.currentStatus: Current is the display label for authored status ready, not a claim that a fresh report arrived in this step and not an automatic freshness calculation. Cached is the label for stale. See rendererReferences.statusLabels.
semantics.updatedBadge: Updated is a per-step changed field or assigned report marker. It is not the physical-state-change timestamp and does not imply a new network message unless the step actually authors one. Reassigning reportedAt can mark a field Updated even if the value is unchanged. See fieldMerge and reportFreshness renderer references.
semantics.reportTime: Only reportedAt is machine-resolved as a report time. Report times carry independently of values. Prose detail is retained verbatim and is not inferred here as a timestamp. Nonempty explicit detail pins its text until a later report without detail; autogenerated relative freshness otherwise ages from the report time. A report timestamp is distinct from when the underlying value last changed. See rendererReferences.reportFreshness.
semantics.notifications: Notifications persist as a newest-first stack. Only a patch with clear:true clears the stack; a notify operation prepends cards. Changing phoneScreen from home to app does not clear notifications. Both phone screens render the stack. Model cards are the first three; count records the full stack. The approved HLD and answer sheets do not specify dismissal-on-open, so retained notifications alone are not evidence of violating a stated dismissal contract. See rendererReferences.notificationStack, homeVsApp and fieldCardVisibility; fixture input/hld.md:59-63.
semantics.homemapSignals: Homemap device state and subject positions carry, but signals never carry. foldHomemapStates excludes signals from carried state and takes a fresh array only from the current step patch; absence means []. Therefore a previous heartbeat or charging signal does not remain at sunrise, a later delivery or retry. At an active step the renderer draws static direction markers even when paused/reduced-motion; moving packets are transient animation. Links shorter than 24 layout units are omitted. See rendererReferences.homemapSignals and homemapSignalMarkers.
semantics.edges: Declared topology is a relationship inventory, not evidence that a message happens at a particular step. activeEdges, deliveredEdges and failures are computed only from that step. edges takes precedence over legacy edge; panels takes precedence over legacy patch. Delivered excludes blocked/dropped failure keys. Past-heartbeat text and an old reportedAt alone do not prove a current heartbeat. See rendererReferences.edgeDelivery.
semantics.battery: Physical battery and app reported values are independent. The physical fold integrates the previous interval trend; explicit charge overrides the result and a drain applies once if there is no charge override. The current trend applies to the following interval. displayGauge rounds the precise folded charge; the zone compares the precise charge. A rounded 20% can therefore remain above a <=20 threshold. See batteryFold and batteryDisplayRounding renderer references.
semantics.clock: Story time advances along the selected path and carries when omitted. Phone clock/date derive from the resolved timeline unless an explicit display override pins them. Business answers specify Thursday around 22:30 and sensible minutes, not a calendar date; engineering answers specify Sep24 22:30 and the listed engineering anchors. See rendererReferences.clockAndDate and approvedEvidenceReferences.

diagrams.heading: Why the resident got a battery alert at night, and why the package alert can come late
prose: One night for a Porch Cam on battery, from 10:30 PM Thursday to Friday morning. Pick an ending: a normal morning, or a morning when the home Wi-Fi is down as the courier arrives.

Clock minutes, the 30-minute check-in times shown and the camera page values between check-ins are illustrative. The battery uses the design's figures: about 1% an hour idle, about 1% per clip, and 3% an hour from the sun (the low end of its 3–4%). Those figures would reach 20% around 2:30 AM, earlier than the ~4 AM alert this story uses, so the battery meter holds at 25% until the 4:00 AM check-in reports 20%.

location.label: heartbeat route
location.purpose: Accepts a heartbeat and writes battery/charging to device-shadow

location.label: motion event route
location.purpose: Accepts a motion event, requests a classification label, and forwards person/package events to notify-service

location.label: clip upload
location.purpose: Stores an uploaded clip, including late uploads from SD card queues

location.label: low-battery rule
location.purpose: Marks low_battery at <=20% and re-arms above 30%; triggers one low-battery push

location.label: offline rule
location.purpose: Marks a device offline after two missed heartbeats (60 min)

location.label: send push
location.purpose: Sends push through APNs/FCM; animal events are skipped by default preference

location.label: device page
location.purpose: Device page: battery %, charging icon, 'updated <time>', online/offline

steps.caption: 10:30 PM Thursday. The resident goes to bed. The Porch Cam is on battery at **25%**, not charging, and everything is online. Every 30 minutes the camera checks in through the home Wi-Fi with its battery level and whether it is charging; the Kestrel cloud keeps that as the camera's status. No alerts on the phone.

1:05 AM. A raccoon crosses the porch. The camera wakes, records a clip of about 20 seconds and uploads it. The clip is sorted as an **animal**: it is saved to the app's timeline, and by default animals do **not** send an alert, so the resident sleeps on.

physicalBattery.note: held at 25%: story times and usage figures disagree
physicalBattery.label: NOMINAL

steps.caption: 4:00 AM. The regular check-in reports the battery at **20%**. That is the low-battery line, so the Kestrel cloud marks the camera low and sends **one** "Porch Cam battery low" alert. It will not send another until the battery is back above 30%. This is the alert a customer asks about in the morning.
6:50 AM. Sunrise. The small solar panel starts charging the battery. Nobody is told yet: the camera will say it is charging at its next check-in.

7:00 AM. The next check-in reports **charging: yes**. From now on the app's camera page shows the solar charging icon. The battery is still under 30%, so the low-battery mark stays on and no new battery alert is sent.
8:10 AM. A courier drops a package. The camera records and uploads the clip through the home Wi-Fi; it is sorted as a **package**, so the resident gets "Package delivered at front door" right away.

8:12 AM. The resident taps the alert. The app reads the camera's status and plays the clip. The camera page shows battery **21%** from the 8:00 AM check-in, charging from the sun, online, and the package as the last event. The battery is back above 20%, but the camera stays marked low until it passes 30%.

foldedState.banner: Clip playing in the Kestrel app

1:05 AM. A raccoon crosses the porch. The camera wakes, records a clip of about 20 seconds and uploads it. The clip is sorted as an **animal**: it is saved to the app's timeline, and by default animals do **not** send an alert, so the resident sleeps on.

physicalBattery.label: NOMINAL

It will not send another until the battery is back above 30%. This is the alert a customer asks about in the morning.
6:50 AM. Sunrise. The small solar panel starts charging the battery. Nobody is told yet: the camera will say it is charging at its next check-in.

7:00 AM. The next check-in reports **charging: yes**. From now on the app's camera page shows the solar charging icon. The battery is still under 30%, so the low-battery mark stays on and no new battery alert is sent.

8:10 AM, but this morning the **home Wi-Fi is down**. The courier drops the package; the camera records the clip anyway and keeps it on its own memory card. It cannot reach the Wi-Fi, so nothing goes to the Kestrel cloud and **no alert** reaches the phone. The camera tries again every 2 minutes.

foldedState.banner: Saved on the camera's memory card · Wi-Fi down

steps.caption: 8:20 AM. The home Wi-Fi is back, about 10 minutes later. On its next try the camera sends the delivery and uploads the saved clip, then checks in. The outage was shorter than an hour, so the camera was never marked offline.

8:20 AM. The clip is sorted as a **package**, and the resident now gets "Package delivered at front door", about **10 minutes late**. The alert was late because the camera could not reach the internet, not because anything in Kestrel failed.
